packet.description_seed: Prosecutors accused 21-year-old student Zyaire Wilkins of publishing on Steam several fake video games that contained malware, infecting thousands of victims, and stealing crypto from some of them.

what: FBI arrests man accused of using Steam games to drain victims’ crypto wallets

clean_source_blocks.text: Prosecutors accused 21-year-old student Zyaire Wilkins of publishing on Steam several fake video games that contained malware, infecting thousands of victims, and stealing crypto from some of them.

U.S. prosecutors have accused a Florida man of uploading fake video games that contained malware to Steam, the popular PC games platform. Once victims downloaded and installed the games, the malware was designed to infect their computers, steal their passwords and other data, and drain their crypto wallets, according to a criminal complaint. On Tuesday, the FBI arrested Zyaire Wilkins, a 21-year-old Florida resident and student. On Wednesday, prosecutors accused him and a number of unnamed co-conspirators of hacking crimes. Over the past two years, Wilkins and his partners allegedly published several malware-laden video games on Steam, including BlockBlasters, Dashverse, Lampy, Lunara, and PirateFi. Using that malware, says the FBI, Wilkins and his accomplices infected around 8,000 victims, and then hacked around 80 cryptocurrency wallets to steal at least $220,000 worth of crypto. ---

A 21-year-old Florida man allegedly hid crypto-stealing malware inside Steam games, robbed thousands of players, and got caught over his Uber Eats orders. Federal agents arrested Zyaire Wilkins of North Lauderdale on Tuesday and accused him of helping run a scheme that put infected games online and quietly emptied players’ crypto wallets. The FBI says the games looked completely normal, which is exactly why so many people downloaded them. As reported by Local10, Wilkins and others launched eight infected games between May 2024 and February 2026, and reached around 8,000 devices and stealing at least $220,000 in crypto.

Zyaire Wilkins is accused of working with co-conspirators to launch and market eight malware-embedded Steam games. Federal authorities have arrested a Florida man suspected of stealing at least $220,000 in crypto through malware-infected Steam games, as reported earlier by local news outlet Local10. In the complaint, officials accuse 21-year-old Zyaire Wilkins and co-conspirators of launching eight malware-embedded games from around May 2024 to February 2026, allowing them to infect about 8,000 devices and gain access to 80 crypto wallets.

Though the complaint doesn’t specifically say the games were uploaded to Steam, it’s likely referring to the Valve-owned gaming platform. As noted by Local10, the FBI put out a call for victim information in a “Steam malware investigation” that includes the games listed in the lawsuit, including BlockBlasters, Chemia, Dashverse/DashFPS, Lampy, Lunara, PirateFi, and Tokenova.

Last year, several outlets also reported on Steam’s removal of some of these cryptostealing games, such as Blockblasters, which took more than $150,000 from victims, including a streamer raising funds for their cancer treatment. The lawsuit is also filed in a Washington court, where Valve is based. Valve didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

The complaint alleges Wilkins and co-conspirators “marketed the malware-embedded video games on social media and messaging platforms, such as Discord, Telegram, X / Twitter, and LinkedIn, and encouraged others to download the games.” From there, authorities allege the conspirators used the malware to steal their victims’ private information and drain their crypto wallets.

Federal agents linked Wilkins to the case after obtaining his crypto wallet address in messages with an alleged co-conspirator. They traced the crypto address to an account on Bitrefill, a site where users can purchase gift cards with crypto. The account tied to Wilkins purchased more than 150 gift cards, including to Uber Eats, which authorities used to uncover his phone number, and eventually, an address.

Wilkins was arrested on July 14th and charged with conspiracy to obtain information by computer for private financial gain.

[Lähde: Dexerto | URL: https://www.dexerto.com/gaming/florida-man-arrested-for-220k-video-game-malware-scam-after-fbi-tracks-his-uber-eats-deliveries-3388181/]
A 21-year-old Florida man allegedly hid crypto-stealing malware inside Steam games, robbed thousands of players, and got caught over his Uber Eats orders.

Federal agents arrested Zyaire Wilkins of North Lauderdale on Tuesday and accused him of helping run a scheme that put infected games online and quietly emptied players’ crypto wallets. The FBI says the games looked completely normal, which is exactly why so many people downloaded them.

As reported by Local10, Wilkins and others launched eight infected games between May 2024 and February 2026, and reached around 8,000 devices and stealing at least $220,000 in crypto.

They pushed the games on Discord, Telegram, X, and LinkedIn, and used bots to find people holding a lot of crypto and nudge them into downloading. Once a game was installed, it grabbed the player’s private data and passwords, which the group then used to break into wallets.

What tripped him up was Uber Eats. Agents followed the stolen crypto to a service that sells gift cards, found more than 150 of them bought mostly for food delivery, and asked Uber where the orders went.

The deliveries led straight to Wilkins’ home and his college addresses. This looks like the first arrest from an FBI investigation that went public in March, when the bureau asked affected players to come forward.

It follows the September case where malware in a Steam game drained a streamer raising money for his cancer treatment, part of a wider run of Steam scares that recently saw hackers hide malware in Wallpaper Engine downloads. As for Wilkins, he will be facing up to 10 years in prison.

payload.title: FBI pidätti Steam-peleihin haittaohjelmia piilottaneeksi epäillyn miehen
payload.summary: 21-vuotiaan Zyaire Wilkinsin ja hänen kumppaniensa epäillään levittäneen Steamissa kahdeksaa saastunutta peliä. FBI:n mukaan noin 8 000 laitetta sai tartunnan, ja ryhmä pääsi käsiksi noin 80 kryptolompakkoon.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain liittovaltion poliisi FBI on pidättänyt 21-vuotiaan floridalaisen opiskelijan Zyaire Wilkinsin, jota syyttäjät epäilevät haittaohjelmia sisältäneiden pelien julkaisemisesta Steamissa ja vähintään 220 000 dollarin arvoisten kryptovarojen varastamisesta käyttäjien sähköisistä lompakoista.

## Kahdeksan peliä vajaan kahden vuoden aikana

Rikosepäilyä koskevan asiakirjan mukaan North Lauderdalessa asuva Wilkins työskenteli useiden nimeämättömien kumppaneiden kanssa. Ryhmän epäillään julkaisseen ja markkinoineen kahdeksan haittaohjelman sisältänyttä peliä toukokuun 2024 ja helmikuun 2026 välisenä aikana. Julkaisuista mainitaan nimeltä BlockBlasters, Dashverse, Lampy, Lunara ja PirateFi. Kaikkia kahdeksaa peliä ei ole aineistossa nimetty.

Steam on suosittu PC-pelialusta. FBI:n mukaan saastuneet pelit näyttivät käyttäjille tavallisilta tietokonepeleiltä. Kun käyttäjä latasi ja asensi pelin, sen mukana tullut haittaohjelma saattoi saastuttaa tietokoneen. Rikosepäilyn mukaan ohjelma oli suunniteltu varastamaan salasanoja ja muita tietoja sekä tyhjentämään käyttäjän kryptovaluuttalompakko.

FBI pidätti Wilkinsin tiistaina. Syyttäjät esittivät häntä ja epäiltyjä rikoskumppaneita koskevat hakkerointisyytökset keskiviikkona. Syytökset koskevat haittaohjelmien levittämistä, niiden avulla tehtyjä tietomurtoja ja kryptovarojen anastamista. Wilkinsin lisäksi asiassa epäillään useita henkilöitä, joiden nimiä ei ole julkistettu.

## Noin 8 000 laitetta sai tartunnan

FBI:n mukaan haittaohjelmaa levittäneet pelit saastuttivat noin 8 000 laitetta. Epäillyn ryhmän väitetään päässeen noin 80 kryptovaluuttalompakkoon ja varastaneen niistä kryptovaroja vähintään 220 000 dollarin arvosta.

Viranomaisten ilmoittamat luvut kuvaavat kahta eri joukkoa: tartunnan saaneita laitteita oli noin 8 000, mutta ryhmän epäillään päässeen noin 80 kryptolompakkoon. Julkaistujen tietojen perusteella ei siten ole selvää, että jokainen haittaohjelman saanut käyttäjä olisi menettänyt kryptovaroja. Tiedoista ei käy ilmi, kuinka monesta lompakosta varoja lopulta siirrettiin tai miten tappiot jakautuivat uhrien kesken. Vähintään 220 000 dollarin summa on tutkinnassa esitetty kokonaisarvio.

Kyse on tässä vaiheessa viranomaisten rikosepäilystä ja rikosasiakirjassa esitetyistä väitteistä. Wilkinsin vastauksesta syytöksiin tai asian seuraavan oikeuskäsittelyn ajankohdasta ei ole kerrottu.
summary_bullets: Epäilty ryhmä julkaisi syyttäjien mukaan kahdeksan haittaohjelmia sisältänyttä peliä Steamissa.
Pelit saastuttivat FBI:n mukaan noin 8 000 laitetta.
Ryhmän epäillään päässeen noin 80 kryptolompakkoon ja vieneen vähintään 220 000 dollarin arvosta varoja.
payload.journalist_note: Viranomaisten väitteet on muotoiltu epäilyiksi. Aineisto ei sisällä Wilkinsin vastinetta eikä kaikkien kahdeksan pelin nimiä.

FBI:n mukaan haittaohjelmaa levittäneet pelit saastuttivat noin 8 000 laitetta. Epäillyn ryhmän väitetään päässeen noin 80 kryptovaluuttalompakkoon ja varastaneen niistä kryptovaroja vähintään 220 000 dollarin arvosta.

Viranomaisten ilmoittamat luvut kuvaavat kahta eri joukkoa: tartunnan saaneita laitteita oli noin 8 000, mutta ryhmän epäillään päässeen noin 80 kryptolompakkoon. Julkaistujen tietojen perusteella ei siten ole selvää, että jokainen haittaohjelman saanut käyttäjä olisi menettänyt kryptovaroja. Tiedoista ei käy ilmi, kuinka monesta lompakosta varoja lopulta siirrettiin tai miten tappiot jakautuivat uhrien kesken. Vähintään 220 000 dollarin summa on tutkinnassa esitetty kokonaisarvio.

Kyse on tässä vaiheessa viranomaisten rikosepäilystä ja rikosasiakirjassa esitetyistä väitteistä. Wilkinsin vastauksesta syytöksiin tai asian seuraavan oikeuskäsittelyn ajankohdasta ei ole kerrottu.

Prosecutors accused 21-year-old student Zyaire Wilkins of publishing on Steam several fake video games that contained malware, infecting thousands of victims, and stealing crypto from some of them.

U.S. prosecutors have accused a Florida man of uploading fake video games that contained malware to Steam, the popular PC games platform. Once victims downloaded and installed the games, the malware was designed to infect their computers, steal their passwords and other data, and drain their crypto wallets, according to a criminal complaint. On Tuesday, the FBI arrested Zyaire Wilkins, a 21-year-old Florida resident and student. On Wednesday, prosecutors accused him and a number of unnamed co-conspirators of hacking crimes. Over the past two years, Wilkins and his partners allegedly published several malware-laden video games on Steam, including BlockBlasters, Dashverse, Lampy, Lunara, and PirateFi. Using that malware, says the FBI, Wilkins and his accomplices infected around 8,000 victims, and then hacked around 80 cryptocurrency wallets to steal at least $220,000 worth of crypto. ---

A 21-year-old Florida man allegedly hid crypto-stealing malware inside Steam games, robbed thousands of players, and got caught over his Uber Eats orders. Federal agents arrested Zyaire Wilkins of North Lauderdale on Tuesday and accused him of helping run a scheme that put infected games online and quietly emptied players’ crypto wallets. The FBI says the games looked completely normal, which is exactly why so many people downloaded them. As reported by Local10, Wilkins and others launched eight infected games between May 2024 and February 2026, and reached around 8,000 devices and stealing at least $220,000 in crypto.

Zyaire Wilkins is accused of working with co-conspirators to launch and market eight malware-embedded Steam games.
